objectives: This study aimed to evaluate the impact of smart healthcare interventions on disease activity, self-efficacy, self-management, functional levels, and quality of life in rheumatoid arthritis (RA) patients, as well as any associated adverse events.
inclusion_criteria: Eligibility criteria were defined using population, intervention, control, outcome, and study design. Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials focused on smart health interventions for adults with rheumatoid arthritis. RA could be defined by established classification criteria (such as the 1987 ACR criteria or the 2010 ACR/EULAR criteria) or by a physician's clinical diagnosis. Eligible interventions included smart healthcare approaches that enabled symptom tracking and self-management support via health applications or online platforms, as well as telemedicine and teleconsultation services; common functions included automated symptom tracking, regular remote follow-up, and self-management support. Studies had to report outcome data specifically attributable to the smart healthcare component.
exclusion_criteria: The accessible main text explicitly excluded studies that did not report outcome data specifically attributable to the smart healthcare component. Under the stated PICOS/RCT eligibility framework, studies outside adult rheumatoid arthritis randomized controlled trials of smart healthcare interventions were also ineligible.
